payload.does: Implement the prescribed approach and AC within the explicitly approved ticket file/directory scope (module if none); reuse existing code. Never expand the ticket scope. If expansion is needed, fail with details.
Run ticket tests and configured checks. Write coder-report.txt to the Artifacts directory named in the workflow prompt. Include changed files, commands, exit codes, AC coverage and blockers.
Unmet AC, failed checks or missing implementation inputs: GATE_FAIL.
Emit OK only when AC and checks pass.

Review the ticket diff read-only against its AC and prescribed approach. Check affected paths and callers. Architecture: contracts/boundaries. Codereview: clarity/duplication. Security: inputs/permissions/secrets. Treat the worktree and its Git index as read-only: no file writes, redirects or git add/stash/checkout/reset/commit there. Write reports and temporary files only to the Artifacts directory named in the workflow prompt.
Name the subject you reviewed in the saved verdict.
HIGH: concrete AC, correctness, security or reliability defect. Optional improvements: MED/LOW. REJECT only HIGH; otherwise CLEAR.
For each finding, record evidence, impact and a concrete fix. Name missing evidence when the fix is unknown. Report checked and unchecked paths.

Read only the assigned ticket, its attachments and applicable repository instructions. Extract prescribed changes, target files and checks. Never expand the ticket scope. If expansion is needed, fail with details.
Verify prescribed changes against current source. Missing implementation inputs or source contradictions: PREMISE_BROKEN.
Use the shared CBM index to check the ticket's named files and symbols against current source. Check SIMILAR_TO before adding a function or module.

Already implemented: DUPLICATE. Use the file/directory scope explicitly approved in the ticket or its current scope attachment; otherwise use the ticket module. Required changes outside that scope: OUT_OF_MODULE.

Write scout.txt to the Artifacts directory named in the workflow prompt. Include verified files, prescribed checks and concrete blockers. Emit the applicable failure signal for a blocker; otherwise OK.
